annotations.SpringBootApplication: Marks the main class. It combines @Configuration (this class can define beans), @EnableAutoConfiguration (Spring Boot configures DB, web server, JSON... based on the jars on the classpath) and @ComponentScan (find @Component/@Service/@Repository/@Controller classes in this package and below).
annotations.RestController: This class handles HTTP requests and every method's return value is written straight into the response body as JSON. It is @Controller + @ResponseBody.
annotations.Controller: A web controller (MVC). Without @ResponseBody, return values are treated as view names (HTML templates).
annotations.RequestMapping: Maps a URL path (and optionally method/headers) to this class or method. On a class it sets a common prefix for all methods, e.g. /api/tasks.
annotations.GetMapping: Handles HTTP GET on this path - GET is for reading data and must not change anything (safe and idempotent).
annotations.PostMapping: Handles HTTP POST - used to create a new resource. Usually answers 201 Created.
annotations.PutMapping: Handles HTTP PUT - replaces a resource completely. Idempotent: sending the same request twice gives the same result.
annotations.PatchMapping: Handles HTTP PATCH - partial update of a resource (only the fields you send).
annotations.DeleteMapping: Handles HTTP DELETE - removes a resource. Usually answers 204 No Content.
annotations.PathVariable: Binds a part of the URL path to this parameter, e.g. /tasks/{id} -> id.
annotations.RequestParam: Binds a query-string parameter (?page=2&size=20) to this method parameter.
annotations.RequestBody: Spring reads the JSON request body and converts it (with Jackson) into this Java object.
annotations.RequestHeader: Binds an HTTP request header to this parameter.
annotations.CookieValue: Binds a cookie sent by the browser to this parameter.
annotations.ResponseStatus: Sets the HTTP status code returned when this method (or exception) completes, e.g. 201 CREATED or 204 NO_CONTENT.
annotations.ExceptionHandler: This method handles the listed exception type(s) thrown by controllers and turns them into an HTTP response.
annotations.RestControllerAdvice: A global helper for all controllers - typically holds @ExceptionHandler methods so error handling lives in one place.
annotations.ControllerAdvice: Global advice for all controllers (exception handling, model attributes).
annotations.Valid: Triggers Bean Validation on this object: all @NotBlank/@Size/@Email... rules are checked before your method runs. Failures become a 400 Bad Request.
annotations.Validated: Enables validation on this class (for @ConfigurationProperties, or method-level validation in a bean).
annotations.NotNull: Validation: the value must not be null.
annotations.NotBlank: Validation: the string must not be null, empty, or only spaces.
annotations.NotEmpty: Validation: the string/collection must not be null or empty.
annotations.Size: Validation: length of a string or size of a collection must be within min..max.
annotations.Min: Validation: number must be >= the given value.
annotations.Max: Validation: number must be <= the given value.
annotations.Email: Validation: the string must look like an email address.
annotations.Pattern: Validation: the string must match this regular expression.
annotations.Future: Validation: the date/time must be in the future.
annotations.Past: Validation: the date/time must be in the past.
annotations.Service: Registers this class as a Spring bean in the service layer - where business logic and transactions live. Spring creates one instance and injects it where needed.
annotations.Component: Registers this class as a Spring bean (a generic managed object). @Service, @Repository and @Controller are specialised versions of it.
annotations.Repository: Marks a data-access bean. Spring also translates database exceptions into its own DataAccessException hierarchy.
annotations.Configuration: This class declares beans with @Bean methods - Java-based Spring configuration.
annotations.Bean: The object returned by this method is registered in the Spring container and can be injected anywhere.
annotations.Autowired: Asks Spring to inject a dependency. With a single constructor this is not needed - constructor injection is preferred because fields can be final and the class is easy to test.
annotations.Qualifier: Chooses which bean to inject when several beans have the same type.
annotations.Primary: When several beans match a type, this one wins by default.
annotations.Value: Injects a value from configuration (application.yml / environment), e.g. @Value("${server.port}").
annotations.ConfigurationProperties: Binds a group of settings (e.g. app.jwt.*) into a type-safe Java object instead of many @Value strings.
annotations.ConfigurationPropertiesScan: Finds and registers every @ConfigurationProperties class in the package.
annotations.Profile: This bean is only created when the given Spring profile (e.g. dev, prod) is active.
annotations.ConditionalOnProperty: This bean is only created when a configuration property has a certain value.
annotations.PostConstruct: Runs once after the bean is created and its dependencies are injected.
annotations.PreDestroy: Runs once before the bean is destroyed (application shutdown).
annotations.Transactional: Runs the method inside a database transaction: everything commits together, or everything rolls back on a RuntimeException. readOnly = true lets the database optimise reads. Note: it only works when the method is called from another bean (through Spring's proxy).
annotations.EnableCaching: Turns on Spring's cache abstraction so @Cacheable/@CacheEvict work.
annotations.Cacheable: Cache-aside: on the first call the result is stored in the cache; later calls with the same arguments return the cached value without running the method.
annotations.CacheEvict: Removes entries from a cache - used after writes so readers do not see stale data.
annotations.CachePut: Always runs the method and updates the cache with the result.
annotations.Scheduled: Runs this method on a timer (fixedRate, fixedDelay or a cron expression).
annotations.Async: Runs this method on a background thread pool; the caller does not wait.
annotations.Entity: This class maps to a database table. Each instance is one row; JPA/Hibernate reads and writes it for you.
annotations.Table: Sets the exact table name (and optional indexes/unique constraints) for this entity.
annotations.Id: This field is the primary key.
annotations.GeneratedValue: The database (or Hibernate) generates the primary key. IDENTITY uses an auto-increment/serial column; UUID generates a random id.
annotations.Column: Customises the column mapping: name, nullable, length, unique, updatable...
annotations.Enumerated: How an enum is stored. Always use EnumType.STRING - ORDINAL stores 0,1,2 and breaks if you reorder the enum.
annotations.OneToMany: One row here relates to many rows in another table (one Order -> many OrderItems). mappedBy points to the field on the other side that owns the foreign key.
annotations.ManyToOne: Many rows here point to one row elsewhere (many OrderItems -> one Order). This side owns the foreign key column. Use fetch = LAZY to avoid loading it unless needed.
annotations.ManyToMany: Many-to-many relationship through a join table. Often better modelled as an explicit join entity.
annotations.JoinColumn: Names the foreign-key column used for this relationship.
annotations.JoinTable: Configures the join table of a many-to-many relationship.
annotations.Version: Optimistic locking: Hibernate increments this number on each update and fails if someone else updated the row first - prevents lost updates.
annotations.CreationTimestamp: Hibernate fills this with the current time when the row is inserted.
annotations.UpdateTimestamp: Hibernate updates this with the current time on every update.
annotations.CreatedDate: Spring Data auditing fills this when the entity is first saved (needs @EnableJpaAuditing).
annotations.LastModifiedDate: Spring Data auditing updates this on every save.
annotations.PrePersist: Lifecycle callback: runs just before the entity is inserted - handy for default values and timestamps.
annotations.PreUpdate: Lifecycle callback: runs just before the entity is updated.
annotations.Embedded: Stores the fields of an @Embeddable value object in the same table.
annotations.Embeddable: A value object whose fields are stored inside the owning entity's table.
annotations.MappedSuperclass: A base class whose fields are inherited by entities (e.g. id, createdAt) without being a table itself.
annotations.Lob: Large object column (big text or binary).
annotations.Query: A custom JPQL (or native SQL) query for this repository method, when a derived method name is not enough.
annotations.Modifying: Marks a @Query as an UPDATE/DELETE statement instead of a SELECT.
annotations.Param: Names a parameter used in a @Query (:name).
annotations.EntityGraph: Tells JPA to fetch the listed relationships in the same query - a fix for the N+1 problem.
annotations.EnableWebSecurity: Turns on Spring Security's web configuration so your SecurityFilterChain bean is used.
annotations.PreAuthorize: Checks an expression before the method runs, e.g. hasRole('ADMIN'). If it fails the caller gets 403 Forbidden.
annotations.AuthenticationPrincipal: Injects the currently logged-in user (or JWT) into this parameter.
annotations.CrossOrigin: Allows browsers on other origins (domains) to call this endpoint (CORS).
annotations.Data: Lombok: generates getters, setters, toString, equals/hashCode and a required-args constructor at compile time. Avoid on JPA entities - equals/hashCode over all fields causes subtle bugs.
annotations.Getter: Lombok: generates getter methods at compile time.
annotations.Setter: Lombok: generates setter methods at compile time.
annotations.Builder: Lombok: generates a builder so you can write Task.builder().title("x").build().
annotations.NoArgsConstructor: Lombok: generates a constructor with no arguments (JPA needs one).
annotations.AllArgsConstructor: Lombok: generates a constructor taking every field.
annotations.RequiredArgsConstructor: Lombok: generates a constructor for all final fields - the usual way to do constructor injection with Lombok.
annotations.Slf4j: Lombok: creates a 'log' field (SLF4J Logger) for this class.
annotations.Override: Tells the compiler this method overrides a method from a superclass or interface - you get a compile error if the signature does not match.
annotations.FunctionalInterface: An interface with exactly one abstract method, so it can be implemented with a lambda.
annotations.Deprecated: This API should no longer be used; a replacement usually exists.
annotations.SuppressWarnings: Silences specific compiler warnings for this element.
annotations.JsonProperty: Jackson: sets the JSON field name for this Java field.
annotations.JsonIgnore: Jackson: never write this field to JSON (e.g. a password hash).
annotations.JsonFormat: Jackson: controls how a date/number is formatted in JSON.
annotations.Test: JUnit 5: this method is a test case.
annotations.BeforeEach: JUnit 5: runs before every test in the class - usually builds fresh test data.
annotations.BeforeAll: JUnit 5: runs once before all tests (must be static unless PER_CLASS lifecycle).
annotations.DisplayName: JUnit 5: a human-readable name shown in test reports.
annotations.ParameterizedTest: JUnit 5: runs the same test with different inputs.
annotations.CsvSource: Supplies rows of CSV values to a @ParameterizedTest.
annotations.Nested: JUnit 5: groups related tests in an inner class.
annotations.ExtendWith: JUnit 5: plugs an extension into the test (e.g. MockitoExtension, SpringExtension).
annotations.Mock: Mockito: creates a fake implementation whose behaviour you control with when(...).thenReturn(...).
annotations.InjectMocks: Mockito: creates the class under test and injects the @Mock fields into it.
annotations.Spy: Mockito: wraps a real object so you can verify or override some calls.
annotations.Captor: Mockito: creates an ArgumentCaptor to inspect arguments passed to a mock.
annotations.MockitoBean: Spring test: replaces a bean in the application context with a Mockito mock.
annotations.MockBean: Spring test (older name): replaces a bean in the context with a Mockito mock. Replaced by @MockitoBean in Spring Boot 3.4+.
annotations.SpringBootTest: Starts the full Spring application context for an integration test.
annotations.WebMvcTest: Test slice: starts only the web layer (controllers, filters, advice) - fast controller tests with MockMvc.
annotations.DataJpaTest: Test slice: starts only JPA components (entities, repositories) - fast repository tests.
annotations.AutoConfigureMockMvc: Adds a MockMvc bean to a @SpringBootTest so you can fire fake HTTP requests.
annotations.Testcontainers: Starts Docker containers (e.g. a real PostgreSQL) for the duration of the tests.
annotations.Container: Testcontainers: this field is a container managed by the test lifecycle.
annotations.ServiceConnection: Spring Boot wires the app to this Testcontainers container automatically (URL, user, password).
annotations.DynamicPropertySource: Adds configuration properties at test runtime (e.g. a container's random port).
annotations.WithMockUser: Spring Security test: runs the test as a fake logged-in user.
annotations.Tool: Spring AI: exposes this method to the LLM as a tool it can decide to call.
annotations.Order: Sets the order in which beans (filters, runners, advice) are applied - lower runs first.
annotations.Import: Imports additional @Configuration classes into this one.
annotations.PageableDefault: Default page size and sort used when the client does not send ?page=&size=&sort= parameters.
annotations.FutureOrPresent: Validation: the date must be today or in the future.
annotations.Nullable: Documents that this value may be null.
annotations.Serial: Marks serialization-related fields/methods (serialVersionUID) so the compiler can check them.

keywords.package: Declares which package (folder) this file belongs to. It must match the folder path under src/main/java.
keywords.import: Makes a class from another package usable by its short name in this file.
keywords.class: Declares a class: a blueprint for objects with fields (state) and methods (behaviour).
keywords.interface: Declares an interface: a contract of methods that classes implement. Spring Data repositories are interfaces that Spring implements for you at runtime.
keywords.record: Declares a record (Java 16+): an immutable data carrier. The compiler generates the constructor, getters, equals, hashCode and toString. Perfect for DTOs.
keywords.enum: Declares an enum: a fixed set of named constants (e.g. TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE).
keywords.extends: Inheritance: this type builds on another class (or interface) and inherits its members.
keywords.implements: This class promises to provide every method of the listed interface(s).
keywords.private: Visible only inside this class - encapsulation. Fields are usually private.
keywords.protected: Visible inside this package and in subclasses. JPA's required no-args constructor is often protected so only JPA uses it.
keywords.static: Belongs to the class itself, not to each object. Shared by all instances.
keywords.final: Cannot change after it is set (for fields/variables), be overridden (methods) or be extended (classes). final fields + constructor injection = immutable, thread-safe services.
keywords.abstract: Cannot be instantiated directly; subclasses must provide the missing parts.
keywords.return: Ends the method and hands a value back to the caller.
keywords.new: Creates a new object by calling a constructor.
keywords.throw: Raises an exception, stopping normal execution until something catches it.
keywords.throws: Declares that this method may throw these checked exceptions, so callers must handle them.
keywords.try: Starts a block whose exceptions can be caught. try (resource) {...} closes the resource automatically.
keywords.catch: Handles an exception of the given type thrown in the try block.
keywords.finally: Always runs after try/catch - used for cleanup.
keywords.if: Runs the block only when the condition is true.
keywords.else: Runs when the preceding if condition was false.
keywords.for: Loop: repeats the block for each element or while a counter condition holds.
keywords.while: Loop: repeats while the condition is true.
keywords.switch: Chooses a branch by value. Modern switch expressions with -> return a value and need no break.
keywords.this: Refers to the current object - e.g. this.repository = repository assigns the constructor parameter to the field.
keywords.super: Refers to the parent class (its constructor or methods).
keywords.var: Local variable type inference: the compiler works out the type from the right-hand side.
keywords.instanceof: Checks an object's type; with a pattern (x instanceof Foo foo) it also casts it.
keywords.synchronized: Only one thread at a time may run this block/method on the same lock - protects shared state.
keywords.volatile: Every thread always sees the latest value of this field (visibility guarantee).
keywords.default: In an interface: a method with a body. In a switch: the fallback branch.
keywords.null: The absence of an object. Prefer Optional or validation over passing null around.

symbols.ResponseEntity: Represents the whole HTTP response: status code, headers and body. Use it when you need control beyond the default 200 OK.
symbols.HttpStatus: Enum of HTTP status codes (200 OK, 201 CREATED, 404 NOT_FOUND...).
symbols.ProblemDetail: Spring's implementation of RFC 9457 - a standard JSON error format (type, title, status, detail).
symbols.JpaRepository: Spring Data interface giving you save, findById, findAll, deleteById, paging and sorting for free. Spring generates the implementation at startup.
symbols.CrudRepository: Spring Data interface with basic create/read/update/delete methods.
symbols.Optional: A box that may or may not contain a value - forces the caller to handle 'not found' explicitly instead of risking a NullPointerException.
symbols.orElseThrow: Returns the value inside the Optional, or throws the given exception if it is empty. A clean way to turn 'not found' into a 404.
symbols.orElse: Returns the Optional's value, or the given default when it is empty.
symbols.ifPresent: Runs the code only if the Optional contains a value.
symbols.stream: Turns a collection into a Stream so you can transform it with map/filter/collect in a declarative style.
symbols.map: Stream/Optional: transforms each element into something else (e.g. entity -> DTO).
symbols.filter: Stream: keeps only elements that match the condition.
symbols.collect: Stream: gathers the elements into a collection or other result.
symbols.toList: Collects stream elements into an unmodifiable List (Java 16+).
symbols.Collectors: Ready-made collectors: toList, toMap, groupingBy, joining...
symbols.groupingBy: Collector that groups elements into a Map by a key.
symbols.forEach: Runs an action for each element.
symbols.List: An ordered collection that allows duplicates.
symbols.ArrayList: Resizable array-backed List: fast random access.
symbols.HashMap: Hash-table based Map: O(1) average lookups; keys need correct equals/hashCode.
symbols.UUID: A 128-bit random identifier - safe to generate anywhere without asking the database.
symbols.LocalDate: A date without time or time zone (2026-10-01).
symbols.LocalDateTime: Date and time without time zone. For timestamps stored in the DB prefer Instant or OffsetDateTime.
symbols.Instant: A point on the UTC timeline - the best type for 'when did this happen' timestamps.
symbols.BigDecimal: Exact decimal numbers - always use it for money, never double.
symbols.Pageable: Page number + size + sort, passed to repositories for pagination.
symbols.Page: One page of results plus total count and page info.
symbols.PageRequest: Builds a Pageable: PageRequest.of(page, size, sort).
symbols.PasswordEncoder: Hashes passwords (BCrypt by default) and checks them - never store plain text.
symbols.BCryptPasswordEncoder: Password hashing with BCrypt: slow on purpose and salted, so stolen hashes are hard to crack.
symbols.SecurityFilterChain: The ordered list of security filters every request passes through; you configure its rules here.
symbols.HttpSecurity: Builder used to configure the SecurityFilterChain: which URLs are public, how users authenticate, CSRF, CORS, sessions.
symbols.OncePerRequestFilter: Base class for a servlet filter guaranteed to run once per request - e.g. a JWT authentication filter.
symbols.UserDetailsService: Spring Security interface that loads a user by username for authentication.
symbols.SecurityContextHolder: Holds the current request's authenticated user (thread-bound).
symbols.Logger: SLF4J logger: prefer log.info("User {} logged in", id) with placeholders over string concatenation.
symbols.SpringApplication: Bootstraps the application: creates the context, runs auto-configuration and starts the embedded web server.
symbols.ChatClient: Spring AI fluent API to talk to an LLM: prompt().system(...).user(...).call().content().
symbols.ChatModel: Spring AI abstraction over a provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama...). Switch providers without changing your code.
symbols.MockMvc: Fires fake HTTP requests at your controllers in tests, without starting a real server.
symbols.assertEquals: JUnit assertion: fails the test if the two values differ.
symbols.verify: Mockito: checks that a mock method was called (and how many times).
symbols.RestClient: Spring's modern synchronous HTTP client for calling other services.
symbols.Clock: Injectable source of the current time - lets tests freeze time.
symbols.MultipartFile: An uploaded file from a multipart/form-data request.
symbols.Cookie: A small value the browser stores and sends back automatically.
symbols.ResponseCookie: Builder for Set-Cookie headers with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Path and Max-Age.
symbols.String: Immutable text. Use equals(), never ==, to compare contents.
symbols.StringBuilder: Mutable text buffer - efficient when concatenating in loops.
symbols.Exception: Base class for errors that can be caught.
symbols.RuntimeException: Unchecked exception: callers are not forced to catch it. Also triggers @Transactional rollback by default.
symbols.IllegalArgumentException: Thrown when a method receives an invalid argument.
symbols.IllegalStateException: Thrown when an object is in the wrong state for the requested operation.
symbols.CompletableFuture: A result that will be available later - lets you compose async work without blocking.
symbols.ExecutorService: A thread pool that runs submitted tasks.
symbols.save: Repository save(): INSERTs a new entity or UPDATEs an existing one and returns the saved instance (now with its generated id).
symbols.saveAll: Repository saveAll(): saves a whole collection, letting Hibernate batch the INSERTs.
symbols.findById: Repository findById(): SELECT by primary key. Returns Optional because the row may not exist.
symbols.findAll: Repository findAll(): SELECT every row - pass a Pageable to fetch one page at a time instead.
symbols.deleteById: Repository deleteById(): DELETE the row with this primary key.
symbols.existsById: Repository existsById(): cheap check whether a row with this id exists.
symbols.created: ResponseEntity.created(uri): builds a 201 Created response with a Location header pointing at the new resource.
symbols.URI: A Uniform Resource Identifier, e.g. /api/tasks/7 - used for the Location header.
symbols.getBindingResult: Holds every validation error found by @Valid, field by field.
symbols.getFieldErrors: The list of fields that failed validation, each with its error message.
symbols.of: Static factory method, e.g. List.of(...) / Map.of(...) create small immutable collections; PageRequest.of(...) builds a Pageable.
symbols.from: Conventional name for a static factory that converts one type into another, e.g. TaskResponse.from(task).

imports.org.springframework.web.bind.annotation: Spring MVC annotations for building REST controllers.
imports.org.springframework.http: Spring's HTTP types: status codes, headers, ResponseEntity, ProblemDetail.
imports.org.springframework.boot: Spring Boot core: bootstrapping, auto-configuration, configuration properties.
imports.org.springframework.data.domain: Spring Data paging and sorting types (Page, Pageable, Sort).
imports.org.springframework.security: Spring Security: authentication, authorization and protection against common attacks.
imports.org.springframework.ai: Spring AI: provider-independent API for LLMs, embeddings, vector stores and tools.
imports.jakarta.persistence: Jakarta Persistence (JPA): the standard annotations for mapping Java classes to database tables. Hibernate implements it.
imports.jakarta.validation: Jakarta Bean Validation: declarative rules like @NotBlank, @Email, @Size.
imports.jakarta.servlet: Jakarta Servlet API: the low-level HTTP request/response model Spring MVC is built on.
imports.javax.persistence: Old (pre-Spring Boot 3) package name of JPA. Spring Boot 3+ uses jakarta.persistence.
imports.lombok: Lombok: generates boilerplate (getters, constructors, builders) at compile time.
imports.org.mockito: Mockito: create mocks and verify interactions in unit tests.
imports.org.testcontainers: Testcontainers: real databases/brokers in Docker for integration tests.
imports.org.slf4j: SLF4J: the logging facade used across the Java ecosystem.
imports.com.fasterxml.jackson: Jackson: converts between Java objects and JSON.
imports.tools.jackson: Jackson 3: converts between Java objects and JSON (Spring Boot 4 default).
imports.io.jsonwebtoken: JJWT: library for creating and parsing JSON Web Tokens.
imports.org.hibernate: Hibernate: the JPA implementation (ORM) Spring Boot uses by default.
imports.java.util.concurrent: Java concurrency utilities: thread pools, futures, concurrent collections, atomics.
imports.java.util: Java core utilities: collections, Optional, UUID...
imports.java.nio: Java NIO: modern file and buffer APIs.

yaml.spring.application.name: The application's name - shows up in logs, metrics and service discovery.
yaml.spring.datasource.url: JDBC connection string of the database: jdbc:postgresql://host:port/database.
yaml.spring.datasource.username: Database user. In production read it from an environment variable, never hard-code it.
yaml.spring.datasource.password: Database password. Keep it out of Git - use ${DB_PASSWORD} environment variables or a secret manager.
yaml.spring.datasource.driver-class-name: JDBC driver class. Usually auto-detected from the URL, so this line is optional.
yaml.spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-si: Maximum number of database connections in the HikariCP pool.
yaml.spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto: What Hibernate does to the schema at startup: create/create-drop (dev experiments), update (risky), validate (production - use Flyway/Liquibase to change the schema), none.
yaml.spring.jpa.show-sql: Prints every SQL statement Hibernate runs - great for learning, noisy in production.
yaml.spring.jpa.open-in-view: Keeps the DB session open during view rendering. Set it to false so lazy-loading surprises happen in the service layer where you can see them.
yaml.spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.dialect: Tells Hibernate which SQL dialect to generate. Usually auto-detected.
yaml.spring.profiles.active: Which profiles are active (dev, prod...). Profile-specific files like application-prod.yml are then loaded too.
yaml.spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size: Maximum size of one uploaded file.
yaml.spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-siz: Maximum size of a whole multipart request.
yaml.spring.threads.virtual.enabled: Serves requests on Java 21 virtual threads - thousands of blocking requests without a huge thread pool.
yaml.spring.cache.type: Which cache implementation to use (caffeine, redis, simple...).
yaml.spring.ai.model.chat: Spring AI: which chat model provider to activate (openai, anthropic, ollama, none).
yaml.spring.ai.openai.api-key: OpenAI API key - always from an environment variable.
yaml.spring.ai.anthropic.api-key: Anthropic API key - always from an environment variable.
yaml.server.port: HTTP port the embedded Tomcat listens on (default 8080).
yaml.server.shutdown: graceful = finish in-flight requests before stopping (important in Kubernetes).
yaml.server.error.include-stacktrace: Whether error responses include stack traces. Keep 'never' in production - stack traces leak internals.
yaml.management.endpoints.web.exposure.includ: Which Actuator endpoints are exposed over HTTP (health, info, metrics, prometheus...).
yaml.management.endpoint.health.show-details: Who may see detailed health info (DB status, disk space).
yaml.logging.level: Log level per package: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR.
yaml.logging.structured.format.console: Prints logs as JSON (ecs/logstash) so log systems like ELK can index fields.
yaml.springdoc.swagger-ui.path: URL of the Swagger UI page that documents your API.

xml.project: Root of the Maven build file (POM = Project Object Model).
xml.parent: Inherits configuration from a parent POM. spring-boot-starter-parent provides sensible defaults and the versions of hundreds of libraries.
xml.groupId: The organisation/namespace of an artifact, usually a reversed domain (com.example).
xml.artifactId: The artifact's name - together with groupId and version it uniquely identifies a library.
xml.version: Version of the artifact. Dependencies managed by Spring Boot's parent do not need a version.
xml.packaging: What the build produces (jar by default).
xml.name: Human-readable project name.
xml.properties: Variables reused elsewhere in the POM, e.g. java.version.
xml.java.version: The Java version to compile for (used by Spring Boot's parent).
xml.dependencies: The list of libraries this project needs.
xml.dependency: One library. Maven downloads it (and everything it depends on) from Maven Central.
xml.scope: When a dependency is available: compile (default), runtime (only when running, e.g. JDBC drivers), test (only in tests), provided.
xml.optional: The dependency is not passed on to projects that depend on this one (common for Lombok).
xml.dependencyManagement: Pins versions (e.g. imports a BOM) without adding the dependencies themselves.
xml.type: The artifact type; 'pom' with scope 'import' imports a BOM (bill of materials).
xml.plugins: Maven plugins that run during the build.
xml.plugin: One Maven plugin. spring-boot-maven-plugin packages an executable 'fat' jar.
xml.relativePath: Empty means 'look up the parent from the repository, not the file system'.
xml.exclusions: Removes transitive dependencies you do not want.
xml.repositories: Extra Maven repositories to download from (besides Maven Central).

artifacts.spring-boot-starter-parent: Spring Boot's parent POM: dependency versions, plugin defaults, Java version handling.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-web: Spring MVC + embedded Tomcat + Jackson JSON: everything for REST APIs.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-webmvc: Spring MVC + embedded Tomcat + JSON (Spring Boot 4 name of the web starter).
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-data-jpa: Spring Data JPA + Hibernate + HikariCP connection pool.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-security: Spring Security: authentication, authorization, protection filters.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-serv: Validate JWT bearer tokens on incoming requests.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-security-oauth2-reso: Validate JWT bearer tokens on incoming requests (Spring Boot 4 name).
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-test: JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito, Spring test support - all test tools in one.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-kafka: Spring for Apache Kafka (Spring Boot 4 name).
artifacts.spring-kafka: Spring for Apache Kafka: KafkaTemplate and @KafkaListener.
artifacts.spring-boot-starter-flyway: Flyway database migrations run at startup (Spring Boot 4).
artifacts.flyway-core: Flyway: versioned SQL migrations for your schema.
artifacts.spring-boot-devtools: Automatic restart and live reload during development.
artifacts.postgresql: The PostgreSQL JDBC driver - lets Java talk to Postgres.
artifacts.h2: In-memory database, handy for quick experiments (not for production).
artifacts.lombok: Generates boilerplate code at compile time.
artifacts.springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui: Generates OpenAPI docs and Swagger UI from your controllers.

sql.CREATE TABLE: Creates a new table with the listed columns and constraints.
sql.CREATE INDEX: Creates an index (a B-Tree by default) so lookups on these columns avoid scanning the whole table.
sql.CREATE UNIQUE INDEX: An index that also forbids duplicate values. With WHERE it becomes a partial index that only covers some rows.
sql.ALTER TABLE: Changes an existing table (add/drop columns or constraints).
sql.DROP TABLE: Deletes a table and its data - irreversible.
sql.PRIMARY KEY: Uniquely identifies each row; implies NOT NULL and creates an index.
sql.REFERENCES: Foreign key: values must exist in the referenced table - the database enforces the relationship.
sql.FOREIGN KEY: Declares a foreign-key constraint linking to another table.
sql.ON DELETE CASCADE: Deleting the parent row automatically deletes rows that reference it.
sql.ON DELETE SET NULL: Deleting the parent sets this foreign key to NULL instead of failing.
sql.NOT NULL: The column must always have a value.
sql.UNIQUE: No two rows may have the same value here.
sql.DEFAULT: Value used when an INSERT does not provide one.
sql.CHECK: A rule every row must satisfy, enforced by the database itself.
sql.VARCHAR: Variable-length text with a maximum length.
sql.TIMESTAMPTZ: Timestamp with time zone (stored as UTC) - the right type for 'when did it happen'.
sql.NUMERIC: Exact decimal number - maps to BigDecimal. Use for money.
sql.JOIN: Combines rows from two tables on a matching condition.
sql.GROUP BY: Aggregates rows into groups (with COUNT, SUM...).
sql.CONSTRAINT: Names a constraint so errors and later migrations can refer to it.

docker.FROM: The base image to build on. 'AS build' names a stage in a multi-stage build.
docker.WORKDIR: Sets (and creates) the working directory for the following instructions.
docker.COPY: Copies files from the build context (or another stage with --from) into the image.
docker.ADD: Like COPY but can also fetch URLs and unpack archives - prefer COPY.
docker.RUN: Runs a command at build time and saves the result as a new image layer.
docker.ENV: Sets an environment variable inside the image.
docker.EXPOSE: Documents which port the app listens on (it does not publish it).
docker.USER: Runs the following commands and the container as this user - never run production containers as root.
docker.ENTRYPOINT: The command that starts the container.
docker.CMD: Default arguments for ENTRYPOINT (or the default command).
docker.HEALTHCHECK: Command Docker runs periodically to check the container is healthy.
docker.LABEL: Metadata attached to the image.

methods.save: Spring Data: INSERTs the entity if it is new, otherwise UPDATEs it, and returns the saved object (with generated id/timestamps).
methods.saveAll: Spring Data: saves every entity in the collection in one go.
methods.saveAndFlush: Saves and immediately sends the SQL to the database (normally it waits until the transaction commits).
methods.findById: Spring Data: SELECT ... WHERE id = ?. Returns Optional because the row may not exist.
methods.findAll: Spring Data: SELECT * from the table (optionally sorted/paged). Careful with big tables - prefer paging.
methods.existsById: Spring Data: SELECT 1 ... WHERE id = ? - cheaper than loading the whole row when you only need yes/no.
methods.deleteById: Spring Data: DELETE the row with this id.
methods.count: SELECT count(*) - how many rows match.
methods.flush: Sends pending INSERT/UPDATE statements to the database now instead of at commit.
methods.orElseThrow: Unwraps an Optional: gives you the value, or throws an exception when it is empty (e.g. 404 Not Found).
methods.orElse: Unwraps an Optional, using the given default when it is empty.
methods.orElseGet: Like orElse, but the default is only created when needed (lazy).
methods.ifPresent: Runs the lambda only when the Optional has a value.
methods.isPresent: true when the Optional contains a value.
methods.isEmpty: true when there is nothing inside (empty string/collection/Optional).
methods.stream: Turns a collection into a Stream so you can filter/map/collect it in a pipeline.
methods.map: Transforms each element (or the Optional's value) into something else, e.g. entity -> DTO.
methods.filter: Keeps only the elements for which the condition is true.
methods.toList: Collects the stream into an unmodifiable List.
methods.collect: Terminal stream operation: gathers the results into a List/Set/Map using a Collector.
methods.forEach: Runs the action once for every element.
methods.sorted: Sorts the stream elements (natural order or with a Comparator).
methods.of: Factory method: creates an immutable List/Set/Map/Optional (or other value) from the arguments.
methods.ofNullable: Wraps a value that might be null into an Optional.
methods.requireNonNull: Throws NullPointerException immediately with a clear message if the argument is null - fail fast.
methods.builder: Starts a builder: set properties step by step, then call build().
methods.build: Finishes the builder and creates the object.
methods.status: Sets the HTTP status code of the response.
methods.created: ResponseEntity.created(uri): HTTP 201 Created with a Location header pointing at the new resource.
methods.noContent: HTTP 204 No Content: success, but no body.
methods.badRequest: HTTP 400 Bad Request: the client sent invalid data.
methods.body: Sets the response body (Jackson turns it into JSON).
methods.encode: PasswordEncoder.encode: hashes the raw password (BCrypt adds a random salt) - never store raw passwords.
methods.matches: PasswordEncoder.matches(raw, hash): checks a login password against the stored hash.
methods.now: Current date/time. Services usually ask an injected Clock so tests can fix 'now'.
methods.plus: Returns a NEW date/time/amount shifted forward - java.time objects are immutable.
methods.minus: Returns a NEW date/time/amount shifted backward.
methods.isBefore: Date/time comparison: true when this moment is earlier.
methods.isAfter: Date/time comparison: true when this moment is later.
methods.equals: Value equality (same content), unlike == which checks same object in memory.
methods.hashCode: Number used by HashMap/HashSet buckets; must agree with equals.
methods.toString: Text form of the object - what you see in logs and the debugger.
methods.strip: Removes leading and trailing whitespace (Unicode-aware trim).
methods.isBlank: true for an empty string or one with only whitespace.
methods.get: Reads a value: from a Map by key, a List by index, or an Optional (throws if empty!).
methods.put: Map.put(key, value): stores/replaces the value for this key.
methods.add: Adds an element to the collection.
methods.remove: Removes an element from the collection.
methods.contains: true when the collection/string contains the element.
methods.getOrDefault: Map lookup with a fallback when the key is missing.
methods.computeIfAbsent: Map: returns the value for the key, creating and storing it first if missing.
methods.merge: Map: combine the new value with the existing one (e.g. counting).
methods.formatted: Fills the %s placeholders of this text block/string with the arguments.
methods.format: String.format: builds a string from a template with %s/%d placeholders.
methods.valueOf: Converts to this type, e.g. String -> enum constant or number -> String.
methods.parse: Parses text into a value (number, date, UUID...). Throws if the text is invalid.
methods.randomUUID: Generates a random, practically unique id (UUID v4).
methods.info: Writes an INFO log line. Use {} placeholders instead of string concatenation.
methods.debug: Writes a DEBUG log line (hidden unless debug logging is on).
methods.warn: Writes a WARN log line - something unexpected but handled.
methods.error: Writes an ERROR log line - something failed.
methods.run: SpringApplication.run: starts Spring - creates the ApplicationContext, all beans and the embedded web server.
methods.assertThat: AssertJ: start a readable assertion, e.g. assertThat(x).isEqualTo(5). The test fails if it is false.
methods.isEqualTo: Assertion: the actual value must equal the expected one.
methods.perform: MockMvc: sends a fake HTTP request through the full Spring MVC stack (no real network).
methods.andExpect: MockMvc: asserts something about the response (status, JSON field, header).
methods.when: Mockito: 'when this mock method is called...' - start of stubbing.
methods.verify: Mockito: checks that a mock method was (or was not) called.
methods.mock: Mockito: creates a fake object whose methods you control in a test.
methods.getContent: Page.getContent(): the list of items on this page.
methods.comparing: Comparator.comparing: sort by a key, e.g. by createdAt.
methods.append: StringBuilder.append: adds text to the end without creating new String objects each time.
methods.substring: Takes part of a string between two indexes.
methods.startsWith: true when the string begins with the given prefix.
methods.endsWith: true when the string ends with the given suffix.
methods.replace: Returns a copy with all occurrences replaced (Strings are immutable).
methods.split: Cuts a string into an array at each match of the regex.
methods.join: Joins elements into one string with a separator.
methods.setStatus: Setter: changes the status field of this object.
methods.authorizeHttpRequests: Spring Security DSL: which URLs need which login/roles.
methods.requestMatchers: Selects URLs (and optionally HTTP methods) for the rule that follows.
methods.permitAll: Anyone may call these URLs, even without logging in.
methods.authenticated: Only logged-in users may call these URLs.
methods.hasRole: Only users with this role (e.g. ADMIN) may call these URLs.
methods.csrf: Configures CSRF protection (usually disabled for stateless token APIs, needed for cookie sessions).
methods.sessionManagement: Configures HTTP sessions - STATELESS means no server-side session, every request carries its token.
methods.addFilterBefore: Inserts your filter into the security filter chain before an existing one.
methods.doFilter: Passes the request on to the next filter (and finally the controller). Forgetting it = request never arrives.
methods.getHeader: Reads an HTTP request header, e.g. Authorization.
methods.setAuthentication: Stores the logged-in user in the SecurityContext for the rest of this request.
methods.getContext: SecurityContextHolder.getContext(): the security info of the current request/thread.

annotationWhy.SpringBootApplication: Without it nothing is scanned or auto-configured: no web server, no beans, no database - main() would just exit.
annotationWhy.RestController: Without it Spring never registers this class's endpoints: every URL here answers 404.
annotationWhy.Controller: Without it the class is not a web controller and its mappings are ignored.
annotationWhy.RequestMapping: Without it every path in this class would have to repeat the common prefix, and a typo in one breaks it.
annotationWhy.GetMapping: Without it no URL leads to this method - it becomes a normal Java method nobody calls.
annotationWhy.PostMapping: Without it the endpoint does not exist and clients get 404/405.
annotationWhy.PutMapping: Without it the update endpoint does not exist.
annotationWhy.PatchMapping: Without it the partial-update endpoint does not exist.
annotationWhy.DeleteMapping: Without it the delete endpoint does not exist.
annotationWhy.PathVariable: Without it Spring does not know to fill this parameter from the {placeholder} in the URL.
annotationWhy.RequestParam: Without it the ?query=value parameter is not bound to this argument.
annotationWhy.RequestBody: Without it Spring does not read the JSON body - the parameter would stay empty/null.
annotationWhy.ResponseStatus: Without it Spring returns the default 200 OK instead of the status this endpoint should send.
annotationWhy.ExceptionHandler: Without it this exception falls through to Spring's default error page instead of your clean JSON error.
annotationWhy.RestControllerAdvice: Without it the @ExceptionHandler methods here only apply to this one class, not the whole API.
annotationWhy.Valid: Without it the @NotBlank/@Size rules on the DTO are NEVER checked - invalid data reaches your service.
annotationWhy.Validated: Without it method-level constraints (@Min on a parameter) are not enforced.
annotationWhy.NotNull: Without it null gets through validation and may crash later with a NullPointerException.
annotationWhy.NotBlank: Without it empty strings and "   " are accepted as valid input.
annotationWhy.Size: Without it very long strings reach the database and fail (or fill it with junk).
annotationWhy.Email: Without it any text is accepted as an email address.
annotationWhy.Service: Without it Spring does not create this bean, so controllers that need it fail at startup with 'No qualifying bean'.
annotationWhy.Component: Without it Spring does not create this bean and injection points for it fail at startup.
annotationWhy.Repository: Without it (and without extending a Spring Data interface) no repository bean is created.
annotationWhy.Configuration: Without it the @Bean methods in this class are ignored - those beans never exist.
annotationWhy.Bean: Without it the returned object is just a local value - Spring never manages or injects it.
annotationWhy.Autowired: Without it (and without a single constructor) Spring does not inject this dependency - it stays null.
annotationWhy.Value: Without it the field is never filled from application.yml - it keeps its Java default (null/0).
annotationWhy.ConfigurationProperties: Without it the yml values are not bound to this class.
annotationWhy.Transactional: Without it each repository call commits on its own: a failure halfway leaves half-written data, and lazy loading may fail.
annotationWhy.Cacheable: Without it every call hits the database again instead of using the cached result.
annotationWhy.CacheEvict: Without it the cache keeps serving stale data after this write.
annotationWhy.Scheduled: Without it this method never runs automatically.
annotationWhy.Async: Without it the method runs on the caller's thread and blocks it.
annotationWhy.Entity: Without it Hibernate ignores this class: no table mapping, and repositories for it fail at startup.
annotationWhy.Table: Without it Hibernate guesses the table name from the class name, which may not match your SQL migration.
annotationWhy.Id: Without it Hibernate refuses to start - every entity needs a primary key.
annotationWhy.GeneratedValue: Without it you must set the id yourself before saving, or the insert fails.
annotationWhy.Column: Without it the column name is derived from the field name and constraints like nullable/length are not declared.
annotationWhy.Enumerated: Without EnumType.STRING the enum is stored as a number (ordinal) - reordering constants would corrupt data.
annotationWhy.ManyToOne: Without it Hibernate does not know this field is a foreign key to another table.
annotationWhy.OneToMany: Without it the collection is not loaded from the related table.
annotationWhy.JoinColumn: Without it Hibernate guesses the foreign-key column name, which may not match your schema.
annotationWhy.Version: Without it two users editing the same row silently overwrite each other (no optimistic locking).
annotationWhy.PrePersist: Without it the defaults/timestamps set in this method are never applied before insert.
annotationWhy.Override: Without it a typo in the method name silently creates a NEW method instead of overriding - @Override makes the compiler catch it.
annotationWhy.Test: Without it JUnit does not run this method at all.
annotationWhy.BeforeEach: Without it the setup does not run before each test, so tests may share dirty state.
annotationWhy.SpringBootTest: Without it no Spring context starts, so autowired beans in the test are null.
annotationWhy.WebMvcTest: Without it there is no MockMvc/controller slice to test against.
annotationWhy.DataJpaTest: Without it there is no repository/database slice for the test.
annotationWhy.MockitoBean: Without it the real bean is used instead of the mock you want to control.
annotationWhy.Mock: Without it the field is null - no fake object is created.
annotationWhy.InjectMocks: Without it the class under test is not created with the mocks injected.
annotationWhy.EnableWebSecurity: Without it your custom security configuration may not be applied.
annotationWhy.Getter: Without it (Lombok) there are no getters, so Jackson cannot serialise the fields and other classes cannot read them.
annotationWhy.Setter: Without it (Lombok) there are no setters to change the fields.
annotationWhy.Data: Without it (Lombok) getters/setters/equals/hashCode/toString are not generated.
annotationWhy.RequiredArgsConstructor: Without it (Lombok) there is no constructor for the final fields, so Spring cannot inject them.
annotationWhy.Builder: Without it (Lombok) the builder() API used elsewhere does not exist.
annotationWhy.NoArgsConstructor: Without it JPA cannot instantiate the entity when loading rows.
annotationWhy.AllArgsConstructor: Without it (Lombok) the all-fields constructor used elsewhere does not exist.
